final:
STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: The shadow-root hiding works for the core cases I probed: nested 2–3 levels, root bounds, stacked cleanup, and top-layer/live-announcer handling. One reproduced gap: content added to an outer call's shadow root is not hidden while a nested call is active, although the equivalent light-DOM addition is. The slotted-child case is a minor gap. The inert path is untested because jsdom has no `inert`.

FILES TOUCHED: packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.probe.test.js was created for the probes and then deleted. `git status` matches the start (the four pre-existing modified files only).

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Nested call stops hiding additions to the outer call's shadow root. Outer targets sit in shadow root A; an inner call with light-DOM targets is then made. Adding an `<input>` to A is not hidden (`hidden=false`), while adding one to body is hidden (`hidden=true`). The inner call only observes body and its own targets' shadow roots, so A goes unobserved until the inner call is cleaned up. This breaks criterion 2 for the outer call. Repro: P15 in the probe file, `expect` on the added node's aria-hidden during the inner call.
- [minor] Light-DOM children of a host on the target's path are hidden even when slotted into the target's shadow tree. Repro: P14, where `<my-host><button>slotted</button></my-host>` with the target inside the host's shadow `<slot>` gets aria-hidden on the slotted button. The criterion's "siblings" wording doesn't clearly cover this. Probably acceptable, but worth a note.
- [minor] shouldUseInert in shadow roots has no real test coverage: `'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype` is false in jsdom, so the `inert` branch never runs (P16 passed only through the aria-hidden fallback).

CHECKS:
- P1 two-level nested siblings hidden, hosts unhidden, light sibling hidden, full restore → pass
- P2 three-level nesting, deep addition hidden, direct and deep additions hidden, restore → pass
- P3 target is a shadow host, its shadow contents untouched, siblings in its root hidden → pass (first run was a probe bug: `<button>` cannot attachShadow)
- P4 nested, inner cleaned, add to shadow root hidden, outer cleanup restores → pass
- P5 non-LIFO cleanup (outer first) → pass
- P6 page pre-hidden aria-hidden stays hidden after revert; addition inside a hidden sibling is not double counted → pass
- P7 root = shadow host containing target: nothing above root hidden → pass
- P8 root inside shadow root, siblings outside root untouched, additions to root hidden → pass
- P9 role=row inside shadow root: target's row not hidden, sibling row and its cell hidden, restore → pass (first run was a probe bug: the row contains the target)
- P10 keepVisible on shadow element, then cleanup and re-hide → pass (first run used the wrong import path)
- P11 top-layer and live-announcer added directly to ShadowRoot stay visible → pass
- P12 closed-mode shadow root target and additions → pass
- P13 cleanup while mutations are pending leaves nothing hidden → pass
- P0 flag off: shadow sibling not hidden, shadow addition not hidden → pass
- P22 stacked: inner targets in shadow root B, inner cleanup, B restored, outer still hides additions to A → pass
- P15 nested call, addition to outer shadow root → FAIL (blocking, reproduced)
- P14 slotted light child of path host → FAIL (minor, reproduced)
- P16 shouldUseInert in shadow root → vacuous (jsdom has no inert)

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should the nested-call gap (P15) be fixed by having the inner call also observe the outer's shadow roots? Or is pausing outer shadow observation during an inner call acceptable? The criteria only say the outer observer resumes on inner cleanup.
